e07s01 — Modal Menu and native-safe mode entry: 12 assessments, PASS
01. Configured mode-key validation accepts case-insensitive F1–F24/none, defaults to F12, and validates the complete configuration candidate before replacement; invalid patches do not commit unrelated settings (src/projects.rs:250–297, 565–612).
02. The retained Ctrl-letter prefix and configured function-key entry are classified before native forwarding without making ordinary native Escape/j/k global commands (src/tui.rs:340–358, 1530–1595, 2180–2425).
03. Explicit F13–F24 events and shifted-lower aliases converge in recognition while extra modifier distinctions are retained; the real parser paths were inspected, not only synthetic key events (src/tui.rs:222–358; vendor/crossterm/src/event/sys/unix/parse.rs:430–451, 619–666).
04. Native encoding covers the accepted upper-key range by converting to managed xterm Shift-F1–F12 sequences rather than returning empty input (src/tui.rs:222–336).
05. Deliberate double-key forwarding requires Press and preceding same-mode entry intent; intervening navigation clears that intent, and Repeat does not become the second deliberate key (src/tui.rs:1524–1595).
06. Both double-key and explicit Actions forwarding use NativeControl input admission; ACP is explicitly refused as a raw native-key destination (src/tui.rs:1560–1575, 2040–2085; src/tui/control.rs:931–958).
07. Menu list/search/action focus are distinct states; j/k/g/G/arrows/Enter perform navigation outside explicit search (src/tui/menu.rs:19–62; src/tui.rs:2190–2385).
08. Search preserves literal j/k/q and bounded pasted text; navigation-mode paste is consumed instead of becoming commands or application input (src/tui.rs:2202–2220, 2230–2375).
09. Rename, launch, project and ACP editors keep literal j/k/? rather than falling through to Menu actions (src/tui/menu.rs:334–451; src/tui/launch.rs:280–414; src/tui/project.rs:697–848; src/tui/agent.rs:1270–1420).
10. Conditional warning handling and ownership-panel interception precede underlying dialogs/application routing; covered input is not buffered for replay (src/tui.rs:1510–1530, 1595–1645; src/tui/control.rs:1380–1440).
11. Menu removal invalidates the physical client canvas once before native rendering; this does not send a clear command to the managed application or replay intercepted input (src/tui.rs:1350–1370; src/tui/view.rs native_surface/draw).
12. Readiness uses explicit Empty/Pending/Inconclusive semantics. Filtered replies, parser fragments, lock contention and bounded yielding do not become an Empty proof (vendor/crossterm/src/event.rs:208–232; vendor/crossterm/src/event/read.rs:44–82; src/tui.rs:1465–1495).

e07s02 — Conversation-first ACP and explicit interaction cards: 12 assessments, PASS
13. Conversation rendering gives the active question/editor priority and puts protocol/settings identities in separate read-only Details/History surfaces (src/tui/agent.rs:1850–2088, 2120–2305).
14. Form, permission, authentication and foreground mutation intent carries painted target, binding, interaction/revision/review phase or foreground/authentication identity; stale hits are rejected before dispatch (src/tui/agent.rs:85–125, 788–817, 973–1100).
15. F5/F6/F7/F8/Ctrl-C and permission Enter route through the same immutable painted-action activation as buttons; there is no surviving compatibility-shortcut bypass (src/tui/agent.rs:1270–1328).
16. New/replaced mutations require successful visible presentation, conclusive Empty and a subsequent armed repaint. The parent does not arm covered ACP controls (src/tui/agent.rs:819–868, 1730–1852; src/tui.rs:1465–1495).
17. Changed target/grant, review phase, foreground, authentication selection, area, hidden/clipped action or covering Help/Details/History invalidates the relevant readiness instead of inheriting previous consent (src/tui/agent.rs:319–385, 788–868, 1855–1875, 2075–2107).
18. Stable same-target prompt paste/Enter and local Review remain immediate; the generalized fence does not introduce blanket double confirmation for ordinary editing (src/tui/agent.rs:70–82, 1000–1030, 1447–1494; immediate-prompt regression).
19. Typed form values are validated through the existing shared validator; Review captures unchanged values and later edits invalidate reviewed submission (src/tui/agent.rs:2880–3027; src/acp.rs:938–968).
20. Exact offered permission option_id, interaction revision and original responder identity survive UI dispatch and broker response construction; no allow/deny inference is added (src/tui/agent.rs:3030–3057; src/acp.rs:976–999).
21. Permission overflow follows focus, unpainted choices do not submit, and oversized context has a bounded scrollable route without truncating the submitted opaque ID (src/tui/agent.rs:1710–1845, 3120–3185; short/many/oversized permission regressions).
22. Completed canonical questions stop lending editable pending intent and return to prompt without discarding canonical history; changed authority discards drafts rather than rebinding them (src/tui/agent.rs:340–381, 554–686; completion and authority regressions).
23. The retained-wrap optimization uses byte/cell ranges only for printable ASCII lines and leaves other lines on grapheme segmentation/Unicode-width accounting. Exact-width endings, blank rows, trailing newline and offsets remain represented; no extra whole-text String copy or context truncation was introduced (src/tui/agent.rs:3604–3656).
24. Permanent wrap coverage asserts semantic slices for ASCII boundaries, blank rows, wide joined emoji and combining marks. The optimization changes no heartbeat threshold, recovery policy, capacity limit or original-effect assertion (src/tui/agent.rs:3841–3855; src/tui.rs:RESUME_GAP/pause_expired; tests/acp/native/acceptance.rs:695–793).

e07s03 — Safe close and identifiable sessions: 12 assessments, PASS

26. Live ACP close captures the complete original ACP tuple, control capability, owner generation and unique call ID (src/tui/menu.rs:189–205).
27. Keep working is the initial close focus, so ordinary first Enter is not destructive consent (src/tui/menu.rs:210–215).
28. Close confirmation depends on complete warning fit and input-empty readiness; clipped/undrawable warnings do not enable confirmation (src/tui/menu.rs:242–272, 530–553; src/tui.rs:1465–1478).
29. Close Help/Escape/resize handling stays local and clears confirmation readiness when returning from Help or resizing; the closing event is not replayed to the application (src/tui/menu.rs:300–353).
30. Detach is a separate action that leaves running work/control semantics intact rather than being translated into close, release or cancellation (src/tui/menu.rs:292–299, 383–398; src/tui.rs:1800–1810).
31. ACP envelopes are forwarded without borrowing a newer grant; daemon authorization and broker exact-target/generation checks remain the actual mutation boundary (src/tui/control.rs:553–580; src/daemon.rs:627–653; src/acp.rs:815–839).
32. Exited native records use remove rather than live-close confirmation, and backend removal refuses a still-live terminal (src/tui.rs:798–810, 2030–2045; src/daemon.rs:1800–1855).
33. Ordinary native exit is shown neutrally instead of as lost ownership; actual exit code and New/Close controls remain available (src/tui/control.rs:721–745, 1525–1536; src/tui/view.rs:493–538).
34. Native/ACP rename validates the complete safe label and mutates runtime naming only; ACP rename preserves its existing broker instance/session/work (src/daemon.rs:1748–1788; src/acp.rs:1148–1156, 2865–2892).
35. Type markers, suffix-based useful names and leaf-preserving native path clipping are present; automatic launch names reserve suffix space within the 128-byte UTF-8 budget (src/tui.rs:445–567; src/tui/launch.rs:135–150; src/daemon.rs:127–150).
36. Replacement selection prefers live native, then live ACP, before retained history; empty-state rendering and input classify both session kinds. The real last-native-removal regression retains the original ACP callback/peer/authority without creating a shell (src/tui.rs:715–749, 811–835, 2230–2245; src/tui/view.rs:580–597; tests/acp/native.rs:1515–1680).

e07s04 — Visible creation and explicit placement: 12 assessments, PASS

38. New checks advertised project_save_terminal:true before either native open or ACP profile catalog/dialog entry. Missing/false support leaves a local full error instead of silently requesting old placement (src/tui.rs:1810–1869).
39. The source session is captured and checked for continuing existence; later Menu selection does not silently become the creation source (src/tui/menu.rs:116–175; src/tui.rs:1810–1828).
40. Current native placement reuses the project; independent native placement allocates a distinct unsaved runtime project after existing source-context capture (src/tui.rs:1855–1870; src/daemon.rs:915–920, 1121–1139).
41. Independent ACP resolves an existing canonical directory and creates a separate unsaved project with no inherited hooks/recipes/main native terminal; it does not mkdir (src/daemon.rs:448–485, 557–574).
42. ACP reservation/admission failures end and clean the unadmitted instance, and independent-project rollback is constrained to an unreferenced unsaved project (src/daemon.rs:536–619; tests/acp/profiles.rs:349–430).
43. Launcher project/profile IDs and model/mode/effort/options are retained exactly; blank overrides inherit profile defaults rather than selecting a substitute provider/model (src/tui/launch.rs:68–180; src/acp_profiles.rs:149–188).
44. Explicit launch names are locally bounded to128 bytes; generated names back up to a UTF-8 boundary and retain their unique suffix (src/tui/launch.rs:135–150, 382–414).
45. Basic/Advanced focus, mouse targets, contextual Help and focused-field scrolling remain local and do not submit pasted text (src/tui/launch.rs:182–381, 470–690).
46. A submitted launch draft freezes while the original FIFO request is pending; buttons do not issue an automatic duplicate launch or cancel an uncertain request (src/tui/launch.rs:230–289; src/tui.rs:1740–1770; src/tui/control.rs:430–453).
47. Typed definite daemon rejection retains the same draft and complete scrollable cause, allowing only a new deliberate attempt; ambiguous transport loss remains fail-closed (src/tui/control.rs:624–675; src/tui/launch.rs:237–249; tests/acp/native.rs:1682–1858).
48. Acknowledged launch identity is captured before follow-up observation and salvaged during fenced teardown; receipt continuity does not replay launch or substitute the previous view (src/tui.rs:1137–1170; src/tui/control.rs:389–425, 697–710; inspected recovery launch consumers).

e07s06 — Consistent controls, authority, status and test quality: 12 assessments, PASS
61. Owned dialogs implement contextual Tab/BackTab, mouse and Escape/Help without routing covered text into native input; ownership warnings/panels paint last and retain interception priority (src/tui.rs:1370–1408, 1595–1810; src/tui/view.rs:160–253).
62. Ordinary Owner intent captures the original grant Arc, generation, observed owner facts and exact manual claim; action matching rejects a replacement grant/request rather than consulting whichever requester is newest (src/tui/control.rs:109–136, 1058–1083, 1740–1795).
63. Both Yield and no-request Release require complete fitted panel/button presentation, Empty, and armed repaint. Keyboard y/r, focused Enter/Space and mouse share that admission; Repeat cannot consent (src/tui/control.rs:1110–1322, 1445–1460, 1890–1997).
64. Owner consent is invalidated by changed authority/request, Help, focus/resize, geometry and clipping; Keep/Return stay local and retain human authority (src/tui/control.rs:1048–1083, 1110–1145, 1290–1322, 1740–1808).
65. Force remains an ownership operation, not implicit interrupt/kill. Ordinary cancellation grants nobody and retains admitted calls; conditional Keep uses the existing original FIFO rather than automatic reacquisition or replay (src/tui/control.rs:1240–1288, 1325–1484, 2037–2095; src/daemon.rs:627–653).
66. Authentication captions consume the real broker method_id/kind projection, not absent name. Full inert selected identity/support context is available through local Help even when button captions need contextual shortening (src/acp.rs:1284–1293; src/tui/agent.rs:130–153, 688–715, 1650–1707, 1800–1830, 1990–2005).
67. F8, Tab/Enter and alternate mouse authentication preserve exact selected method identity. Non-agent methods have no auth/URL/credential/process effect, and broker admission independently checks exact advertised agent support (src/tui/agent.rs:1045–1070, 1280–1300, 1550–1579; src/acp.rs:873–906; tests/acp/native.rs:1275–1515).
68. First same-instance null-to-session establishment preserves read-only Details/History while clearing mutations; full target replacement still resets unrelated state. The recovery consumer retains original tuple/PID/effect checks rather than relying on automatic pane closure (src/tui/agent.rs:332–390; tests/acp/native/recovery_edges.rs:475–571).
69. Attention counts canonical pending, unsubmitted questions/permissions separately from lifecycle/foreground and terminal outcomes. Ordinary snapshots do not acquire transcript/authentication/argv fields from this UX metadata addition (src/acp.rs:329–365, 1243–1268; src/daemon.rs:285–317; src/tui.rs:503–520).
70. Untrusted agent text/options/identities use bounded inert escaping for terminal controls/bidi; response construction retains the exact original opaque IDs. Profile launch remains bounded argv, while hook/recipe shell execution remains an explicitly configured existing feature, not inferred from rendered text (src/tui/agent.rs:3737–3813; src/acp.rs:976–999; src/acp_profiles.rs:69–105, 149–188; src/daemon.rs:943–989; README hooks contract).
71. Regression quality is behavioral: stopped-real-TUI queued F5/permission/Owner cases order original-connection receipts and assert no premature effect, unchanged original authority/work/RPC/PID, then one fresh deliberate effect. Authentication tests use actual broker-shaped payloads and method-specific45/49 arithmetic; the corrected readiness driver distinguishes selected and genuinely inactive styles rather than merely unequal colors (tests/acp/native.rs:727–1515; src/tui/control.rs:2457–2633).
72. Cleanup assertions distinguish normal teardown from failure fallback and observe TUI exit/termios/drainer, owned peer/daemon/socket/root and unrelated sentinel. Retained-capacity correction/cancel assertions remain intact; recovery diagnostics add only a bounded existing-screen excerpt. Implementation continues the existing local module/RPC/configuration patterns; no supported actionable Fowler smell or speculative abstraction recommendation was identified (tests/acp/native.rs:287–322, 475–669; tests/acp/native/acceptance.rs:695–793).
